description: Patch releases are automerged here, on the strength of what the Molecule suite checks and what Vikunja's patch releases have actually contained.

Vikunja is past 1.0 and keeps to semver, and the patch releases of the 2.x line are maintenance-only: 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 (both 2026-03-23) were security releases - nine security fixes plus bugfixes, with 2.2.2 following three days later to complete one of them - and neither carried a schema migration, a breaking change or a config change. These are exactly the bumps that are worse for sitting unmerged than for landing unattended.

Unlike the lago and lldap roles in this fleet, there is no second failure mode stacked on top. `vikunja_version` names one image and one tag (`vikunja/vikunja:<version>`, no flavour suffix), so there is no possibility of Renovate proposing a version that only some of the images this role pulls have been published under.

The one thing that does argue the other way is that the container migrates its own database on startup, forward-only, and that database holds the users' projects and tasks. That is why the Molecule suite has to earn this: it runs every scenario against all three supported backends (SQLite, Postgres, MariaDB) on two distributions, and a bump only merges if, on each of them, migrations complete and the API is actually served (a Vikunja that cannot reach its database stays `active` forever without ever serving, so this is a real gate), the running build reports the pinned version from two independent leaves, the env file demonstrably reaches the process, the role's own `user create` still works against the new binary, a JWT login succeeds, and a project and task written over the API are found in the configured backend with no SQLite fallback alongside it.
Minor and major bumps still require review, which is where a migration or a behavior change would realistically arrive.

On the annotation in defaults/main.yml: `versioning=semver` is load-bearing. `vikunja/vikunja` publishes `latest` and `unstable` channel tags alongside truncated ones (`2`, `2.5`). None of those are valid semver versions, so under `semver` they drop out as candidates and only the full `X.Y.Z` tags remain - which is the intent. No `extractVersion` is needed, as the tags carry no flavour suffix.
